graders.name: window-per-billing-interval
graders.criteria: Reading the code, the system prompt built for a monthly customer gives a 14-day (fourteen-day) refund window from the last charge and the one built for an annual customer gives 30 days: either both rules are stated in the prompt alongside the customer's billing interval, or the code picks the right window per customer. The old flat 'within 30 days' rule for all customers is gone.

graders.name: rest-of-prompt-kept
graders.criteria: Everything else in the prompt is kept with the same meaning: the persona, the customer context interpolations (name, plan and billing interval, member since, last charge), the brevity and knowledge-base guidance, delivery tools, no promised delivery dates, using create_refund_request with billing-team approval in 1-2 business days, never issuing partial refunds or credits, and the numbered knowledge-base snippets.

graders.name: tool-description-fixed-or-flagged
graders.criteria: Passes if either: (a) the create_refund_request tool description (which the model also reads) no longer states a flat 30-day window for every charge and agrees with the new rule (14 days from the last charge on monthly plans, 30 on annual); separating refund eligibility from opening an exception-review request, which docs/policies/refunds.md allows outside either window, is welcome but not required; or (b) the final message accurately points out that the tool description still conflicts with the new rule.

graders.name: change-scoped-to-refunds
graders.criteria: The change stays scoped to the refund window: it does not add unrelated new behaviours or rewrite the prompt's other sections.
